definition: An enthalpy cycle, based on Hess's law, showing that forming an ionic compound from its elements has the same enthalpy change as atomizing the elements, ionizing the atoms and forming the lattice from the gaseous ions; it is used to find a lattice enthalpy or any other missing step.
The enthalpy change when one mole of gaseous atoms is formed from an element in its standard state, such as $\ce{1/2Cl2(g) -> Cl(g)}$; it is positive.
